QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_5

question.text: In a Logical Framework Matrix (LFM), what does 'Objectively Verifiable Indicator' (OVI) require?

answer.text: An indicator that only the SE's internal team can verify
An indicator recorded only in the SE's internal MIS and not shared with the SIA
An indicator that is verified only during the final year of the project
A measurable or observable indicator, defined at project design with a reliable means of verification, so that any independent assessor can verify it using the agreed data source

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook requires KPIs to be objectively verifiable and supported by clearly defined means of verification, with measurable indicators and reliable data sources set at project design. This allows any independent party to use the agreed source to verify the indicator. The Trap: Option A contradicts the 'objectively' requirement. Option C confuses an OVI with end-of-project evaluation timing. Option B describes withheld internal KPIs, which still need to be objectively verifiable if relied upon. Note: The objectively verifiable test sits with the indicator and its means of verification, not with who collects the data.
